title: Random Gaussian Augmented Matrix Product States
authors: Stavya Puri, Poetri Sonya Tarabunga, Piotr Sierant
abstract: Strong entanglement limits the reach of tensor-network descriptions of quantum many-body systems. We study Gaussian-augmented matrix product states (GAMPS), formed by applying a free-fermionic (Gaussian) unitary to a matrix product state. To explore the capabilities of this family, we consider random GAMPS}, a minimally structured ensemble obtained by independently sampling random matrix product states and Gaussian unitaries. Exploiting the algebraic structure of Gaussian unitaries, we develop a replica tensor-network method that computes averages over the random GAMPS ensemble for hundreds of qubits. Random GAMPS exhibit nearly maximal volume-law entanglement already at modest bond dimension, while other quantum resource quantifiers rapidly approach Haar-random state values as the bond dimension increases. The entanglement scaling suggests an exponential reduction in the bond dimension needed to approach the volume-law entropy compared with unaugmented matrix product states. We find a state two-design behavior of random GAMPS at fixed accuracy with a bond dimension independent of system size. Our results reveal how Gaussian augmentation expands the expressive power of tensor networks.
summary: This work investigates Gaussian-augmented Matrix Product States (GAMPS) to understand how adding free-fermionic structure enhances the entanglement capacity of tensor networks. Using a replica tensor-network method, the authors show that random GAMPS rapidly achieve volume-law entanglement, requiring exponentially smaller bond dimensions than standard MPS to reach the same level of quantum resource saturation. This demonstrates a significant expansion in the expressive power of these tensor network descriptions.
main_problem: The study aims to quantify how Gaussian augmentation expands the expressive power of Matrix Product States (MPS) by analyzing Gaussian-augmented Matrix Product States (GAMPS).
main_result: Random GAMPS exhibit nearly maximal volume-law entanglement entropy even at modest bond dimension, suggesting an exponential reduction in bond dimension needed compared to unaugmented MPS.
method: The authors developed a replica tensor-network method to compute ensemble averages over random GAMPS, utilizing a two-copy density operator approach.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by random GAMPS, defined as $|\Psi_Gangle = U_G |\Phi_\chiangle$, where $U_G$ is a fermionic Gaussian unitary and $|\Phi_\chiangle$ is a random MPS.
key_observables: Annealed Rényi-2 entanglement entropy density, Subsystem purity, second-order inverse participation ratio ($I_2$), and state two-design distance ($D_H$).
important_parameters: Bond dimension ($\chi$), system size ($N$), and the crossover bond dimension ($\chi_c$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the ability to compute averages using the quadratic dependence of the quantifiers on the density matrix $ho_G$, and relies on the structure of the fermionic commutant for the Gaussian average.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the GAMPS construction, the contraction method for calculating averages, and show the Page curve demonstrating near-Haar entanglement at modest bond dimensions.
paper_structure: The paper develops the replica tensor-network framework to calculate ensemble averages, analyzes the scaling of entanglement and resource quantifiers across three regimes based on bond dimension, and confirms the enhanced expressive power of GAMPS.
why_interesting: The enhanced entanglement scaling and approach to Haar-random limits suggest that incorporating fermionic structure (Gaussian unitaries) provides a powerful, resource-efficient way to model highly entangled quantum states relevant to strongly correlated electron systems.
